papers.title: Attention-Guided Transformer Network for Polyp Segmentation in Colonoscopy Images
papers.abstract: Polyp segmentation is crucial for early colorectal cancer diagnosis. We propose a transformer-based network with a multi-scale attention decoder. Experiments on three public datasets show a Dice score of 0.923 on Kvasir-SEG and 0.891 on CVC-ClinicDB.

papers.title: Efficient U-Net with Depthwise Separable Convolutions for Real-Time Polyp Segmentation
papers.abstract: Real-time polyp segmentation remains challenging. We propose EfficientU-Net, a lightweight CNN using depthwise separable convolutions. Achieves 0.891 Dice on Kvasir-SEG at 120 FPS with only 2.1M parameters.

papers.title: Cross-Domain Polyp Segmentation via Style Transfer and Domain Adaptation
papers.abstract: Models trained on one colonoscopy dataset often fail on images from different centers. We propose a domain adaptation framework using style transfer. Shows 12% improvement when transferring from Kvasir-SEG to ETIS-Larib.

papers.title: SAM-Med2D: Adapting Segment Anything Model for Medical Image Segmentation
papers.abstract: We adapt the Segment Anything Model (SAM) to medical images by fine-tuning on a large-scale medical dataset. SAM-Med2D achieves 0.812 Dice on polyp segmentation and generalizes across 10 medical imaging modalities.

papers.title: Semi-Supervised Polyp Segmentation with Consistency Regularization and Pseudo-Labeling
papers.abstract: Manual annotation of polyps is time-consuming. We propose a semi-supervised method using consistency regularization and pseudo-labeling that achieves 0.872 Dice using only 20% labeled data, reducing annotation effort by 80%.
